chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about the deceased, so he said: 'Place him in the grave starting from the direction of the feet, and press the earth against the sides of the grave to a height of four spread fingers, and square his grave.'

key_terms.مُفَرَّجَاتٍ: spread/open (referring to the width of the fingers)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended steps for placing the deceased in the grave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* details the precise physical preparation of the grave (*lading*) according to the Imams, emphasizing the creation of a *ladd* (side niche) by pushing earth aside to a depth of four fingers to house the body laterally. The instruction to 'square' the grave (*tarba'*) reflects the traditional Shia practice of constructing a raised, rectangular platform, distinguishing it from simple pit burials and ensuring the deceased rests comfortably in preparation for the questioning of the angels. This ritual underscores the Shia emphasis on dignified, structured burial practices derived directly from the Ahl al-Bayt.
